title: ACT ON PROMOTION OF IMPROVEMENT OF LEVEL CROSSINGS
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to prevent traffic accidents and facilitate the smooth flow of traffic by promoting grade separation or structural improvements of existing level crossings and by providing grade separation at crossings of railroads and roads where new railroads or roads are constructed or existing routes are improved.

Article 2 (Definitions)
The terms used in this Act are defined as follows: <Amended on January 14, 2014.>
1. "Railroad" means a railroad under subparagraph 1 of Article 3 of the Framework Act on Railroad Industry Development;
2. "Road" means any of the following roads:
(a) A road under Article 2 (1) 1 of the Road Act (including a road to which that Act applies mutatis mutandis under Article 108 thereof);
(b) A rural road under Article 2 (1) of the Act on the Maintenance of Roads in Agricultural and Fishing Villages (hereinafter referred to as a "rural road");
3. "Level crossing" means a place where a railroad and a road cross each other at the same grade;
4. "Railroad facility manager" means a railroad facility manager under subparagraph 9 of Article 3 of the Framework Act on Railroad Industry Development;
5. "Road management authority" means a person who manages roads pursuant to Article 20 of the Road Act or maintains rural roads pursuant to Article 5 of the Act on the Maintenance of Roads in Agricultural and Fishing Villages;
6. "Grade separation" means installing an underpass or a road passing over the railroad within a level-crossing section;
7. "Structure" means the materials of the road surface at a level crossing, the gradients and curves of roads and railroads before and after the crossing, the visibility of approaching trains, and other relevant features.

Article 3 (Management of Level Crossings)
(1) A person who has borne expenses pursuant to Article 8 shall be responsible for the maintenance, repair and management of the relevant level crossing: Provided, That level crossings installed before February 5, 1973 shall be managed by the railroad facility manager.
(2) Matters necessary for the management of level-crossing facilities, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 4 (Designation of Level Crossings for Improvement)
(1) Where the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport or a Special Metropolitan City Mayor, Metropolitan City Mayor, Special Self-Governing City Mayor or Do Governor (hereinafter referred to as a "Mayor/Do Governor") deems it necessary to provide grade separation at an existing level crossing or to improve its structure to prevent traffic accidents and facilitate smooth traffic flow, the Minister or Mayor/Do Governor shall designate it as a level crossing for improvement after consultation with the relevant administrative agencies. In such cases, a Mayor/Do Governor may designate a level crossing for improvement only where the entire expenses are to be borne by the Mayor/Do Governor or by a Mayor of a Si, head of a Gun or head of a Gu (meaning the head of a self-governing Gu) pursuant to Article 8 (1).
(2) Where the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport or a Mayor/Do Governor designates a level crossing for improvement pursuant to paragraph (1), the Minister or Mayor/Do Governor shall notify the railroad facility manager and road management authority thereof and publicly notify the designation.
(3) Matters necessary for the criteria for designating level crossings for improvement shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 5 (Establishment of Plans for Improvement of Level Crossings)
(1) Where a railroad facility manager and a road management authority are notified of the designation of a level crossing for improvement pursuant to Article 4 (2), they shall establish a plan for providing grade separation at, or improving the structure of, the relevant level crossing (hereinafter referred to as a "level-crossing improvement plan") and obtain approval from the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport or the relevant Mayor/Do Governor who designated the crossing for improvement pursuant to Article 4 (1). The same shall apply where they intend to amend matters already approved.
(2) Before approving a level-crossing improvement plan under paragraph (1), the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport or the Mayor/Do Governor shall consult with relevant administrative agencies.
(3) Matters necessary for establishing level-crossing improvement plans, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) and (2), shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 6 (Implementation of Improvements to Level Crossings)
A railroad facility manager or road management authority shall provide grade separation at an existing level crossing or improve its structure in accordance with a level-crossing improvement plan approved by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport or the Mayor/Do Governor.

Article 7 (Grade Separation When Constructing Railroads, etc. or Improving Routes)
(1) Where a railroad or road is newly constructed or its route is improved across an existing railroad or road, the point at which the railroad and road intersect shall be grade-separated: Provided, That this shall not apply to cases at or below the standards prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) Matters necessary for standards for grade separation and for construction of intersecting sections when a railroad or road is newly constructed or its route is improved under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 8 (Bearing of Expenses)
(1) Expenses incurred in providing grade separation at an existing level crossing or improving its structure pursuant to a level-crossing improvement plan shall be borne by the following persons: <Amended on November 19, 2014; and July 26, 2017.>
1. Where grade separation is provided:
(a) For an expressway, general national highway, Special Metropolitan City road or Metropolitan City road: The road management authority;
(b) For a road other than those specified in item (a): The person prescribed by joint Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety and the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.
2. Where the structure is improved:
(a) For the connecting railroad: The railroad facility manager;
(b) For the connecting road: The road management authority.
(2) Expenses incurred in providing grade separation when a railroad or road is newly constructed or its route is improved across an existing railroad or road shall be borne by the following persons:
1. Where a railroad is newly constructed or the railroad route is improved across an existing road: The railroad facility manager;
2. Where a road is newly constructed or the road route is improved across an existing railroad: The road management authority.

ADDENDUM <Act No. 11793, May 22, 2013>

This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.
